strings.d1.theme: Kaleiçi classics: Roman gate to meyhane
strings.d1.s0.name: Hadrian's Gate (Üçkapılar)
strings.d1.s0.tips: The three-arched gate dates from AD 130 and is the classic starting point for a guided Kaleiçi walk; the tour continues to the Fluted Minaret, the Broken Minaret, the Clock Tower and the Yacht Marina. A 09:30 start is ideal for both light and cooler air. Look through the glass floor panel under the arch at the Roman paving stones. Book a day ahead; if the group is small, the guide will also take you into Kaleiçi's hidden garden courtyards.
strings.d1.s1.name: Can Can Pide Restaurant
strings.d1.s1.tips: A genuine tradesmen's lokanta in Haşim Işcan neighbourhood, 10 minutes' walk from Kaleiçi; locals call it the best value for money in town. Order the stone-oven pide with minced meat and kaşar cheese and the dish of the day from the pots (kuru fasulye, güveç), and don't skip the chicken soup. The pots run out after 13:00, so come early; cash only.
strings.d1.s2.name: Mermerli Beach
strings.d1.s2.tips: A historic 30-metre beach at the foot of Kaleiçi's walls, right beside the Yacht Marina: sea with mountain views in the middle of the city. In the 2026 season entry is 800 TL including sunbed and towel, reached by the stairs of Mermerli Restaurant. Spend the midday heat in the water here; it is clean, gets deep quickly and there are no crowds of kids.
strings.d1.s3.name: Hıdırlık Tower
strings.d1.s3.tips: A 2nd-century Roman tower at the cliff edge of Karaalioğlu Park; the interior is closed but the surroundings are free, 24 hours. For sunset, claim a spot at the north-west-facing railing at 19:45, when the sun sinking behind the Beydağları mountains turns Konyaaltı Bay orange. Bring a simit (sesame bread ring) and buy tea from the park's tea stand; locals jog here while tourists take photos.
strings.d1.s4.name: Ayar Meyhane
strings.d1.s4.tips: A meyhane (tavern) in the Kılınçarslan streets of Kaleiçi, recognised by the Michelin-style gastronomy guide and also popular with locals. From the cold meze, go for fava, sea beans and octopus salad; ask for fried calamari as the warm starter and ask what the fish of the day is for the main. There is live fasıl music on Friday and Saturday and tables are hard to find, so call and reserve.
strings.d1.b0.name: Kaleiçi Meyhane
strings.d1.b0.tips: A courtyard meyhane in a restored Ottoman house in Kaleiçi; pick from the meze tray, and the Antalya piyaz and steamed sea bass are good. Reservations recommended; there is live music at weekends.
strings.d1.b1.name: Suna-Inan Kıraç Kaleiçi Museum
strings.d1.b1.tips: Two restored Kaleiçi mansions and the former Church of St George house Çanakkale ceramics and recreated Antalya bridal rooms. Closed Wednesday; in summer it closes for a break from 12:00 to 14:00, then reopens until 19:30.
strings.d2.s0.name: Antalya Fishing Harbour
strings.d2.s0.tips: A working fishing harbour run by two fisheries cooperatives in Liman neighbourhood, Konyaaltı; coastal boats dock around 08:30 and the cooperative counter sells that morning's red mullet, sea bream and squid. No sales on Sunday. It is a fishermen's scene, not a tourist one: chat with the men mending nets and have tea from the tea stand. If you buy fish, ask for ice; instead of going to Şişçi Ramazan in the evening you can cook it at a seaside picnic.
strings.d2.s1.name: Konyaaltı Beach
strings.d2.s1.tips: The 7 km pebble beach that makes Antalya what it is, with the wall of the Beydağları mountains behind; the public beach sections are free and sunbeds cost 200-300 TL. The western end by the harbour (near Boğaçayı) is much quieter than the centre, and the water is clearer. Sea shoes help, as the pebbles burn in the heat.
strings.d2.s2.name: 7 Mehmet
strings.d2.s2.tips: Run by the Akdağ family since 1937, this is one of Antalya's long-established restaurants, inside Atatürk Culture Park with cliff views. Its signature pair is lamb tandır on almond iç pilav and piyaz with tahini; don't skip the kabak tatlısı (candied pumpkin dessert) with kaymak and tahini (450 TL). It opens at 12:00 for lunch; ask for a window table for the shaded terrace.
strings.d2.s3.name: Beach Park Antalya
strings.d2.s3.tips: The tree-lined section of the Konyaaltı seafront promenade with cafés; spend the hottest hour in the shade with a coffee, then swim a second time at 17:30. Renting a bike and pedalling along the coast road to Boğaçayı is a local habit. Don't pay for beach club entry; walk down the side streets to the free beach.
strings.d2.s4.name: Konyaaltı Varyant Viewing Terrace
strings.d2.s4.tips: A terrace on the winding road that descends from the centre to Konyaaltı; the whole bay, the Beydağları mountains and the beach in a single frame. The municipality's flowery 'living frame' photo spot is here. Arrive 20 minutes before sunset, because locals with tripods claim the spots. Reach it by KC-line bus or on a 20-minute walk from Kaleiçi.
strings.d2.s5.name: Şişçi Ramazan (Altınkum)
strings.d2.s5.tips: In Konyaaltı Altınkum, the stronghold of Antalya-style şiş köfte; thin skewers cooked over embers come with tahini piyaz, roasted peppers and ayran. One portion of şiş köfte, one portion of lamb şiş and piyaz is enough for two, with kabak tatlısı to finish. Locals crowd in after 20:00 and a 15-minute wait is normal; cards accepted.
strings.d2.b0.name: Konyaaltı Fish Restaurant
strings.d2.b0.tips: The most talked-about fish restaurant in Konyaaltı, with top-class meze. Choose the fish of the day from the counter; the stuffed calamari and grilled octopus are especially good. Reservations are essential at weekends.
strings.d2.b1.name: Antalya Aquarium
strings.d2.b1.tips: A 131-metre tunnel aquarium in Konyaaltı, an air-conditioned alternative for the midday heat. Tickets cost more at the box office and are discounted online; the Snow World section costs extra.
strings.d3.theme: East side: Perge to the waterfall
strings.d3.s0.name: Perge Ancient City
strings.d3.s0.tips: In Aksu, 17 km from the centre; with its Roman-era colonnaded street, central water channel and 12,000-seat stadium, it is the most impressive open-air museum in the region while the Antalya Museum is closed. In summer it opens at 08:00 and the ticket office closes 30 minutes before closing time; there is no shade after 10:30. Foreign visitors pay 11 €; if you are a Turkish citizen, the 200 TL Museum Pass (Müzekart) also gets you into Termessos and Olympos for free.
strings.d3.s1.name: Meşhur Aksu Köfte Piyaz
strings.d3.s1.tips: On Sakarya Boulevard in Aksu district, beside the Antalya-Mersin road; this is the address Antalya locals leave the city for when they want a 'real köfte piyaz'. The köfte is just meat and salt, served as a set with tahini piyaz, roasted peppers, onion, pide and ayran. Come early for lunch; after 13:00 truckers and tradesmen fill the place.
strings.d3.s2.name: Lara Public Beach
strings.d3.s2.tips: A free public beach of golden sand, 2 km long, in Güzeloba; set against Konyaaltı's pebbles, it is Antalya's only long sandy beach. The ministry's public beach section has showers and changing cabins, and sunbeds are 250-300 TL if you want one. There is little shade in the heat, so bring an umbrella; a light breeze picks up in the afternoon.
strings.d3.s3.name: Lower Düden Waterfall (Düden Park)
strings.d3.s3.tips: The point where the Düden Stream drops straight into the sea from a 40-metre cliff; one of the few waterfalls in the world that falls into the sea. Düden Park in Lara is free and open 24 hours, and the best light comes from the west-facing platform just before sunset. For a rainbow in the spray, go down to the lower railing at the right-hand end of the park.
strings.d3.s4.name: Hacı Meyhane Lara
strings.d3.s4.tips: A local ocakbaşı-meyhane (grill counter and tavern) in Çağlayan neighbourhood, behind the hotel district of Lara; rated 4.5 on Tripadvisor yet missing from tourist lists. From the grill, order liver skewers and lamb ribs, and from the meze, spicy ezme and haydari; it is a long-table rakı culture. There is acoustic music at weekends; message them on Instagram to reserve.
strings.d3.b0.name: Barınak Fish House
strings.d3.b0.tips: An air-conditioned neighbourhood fish house in Çağlayan; the daily fish is chosen from the counter and meze prices are half those of the seafront restaurants. Grilled sea bass and shrimp güveç stand out.
strings.d3.b1.name: Kurşunlu Waterfall Nature Park
strings.d3.b1.tips: In Aksu, 10 minutes from Perge; an 18-metre waterfall and turquoise pools inside a pine forest, 5-6 degrees cooler in the midday heat. Entry is about 75-100 TL; swimming is forbidden but you can dip your feet.
strings.d4.s0.name: Balbey Neighbourhood
strings.d4.s0.tips: The first neighbourhood Turks settled in after Kaleiçi; around the Seljuk Balbey Mosque, restored bay-windowed houses stand beside renovation sites in a fabric nobody tours. Early morning gives the best light; have tea at the neighbourhood café and talk to the craftsmen. It is a 5-minute walk north of Kaleiçi towards Şarampol.
strings.d4.s1.name: Erdal Inönü City Park Cliff Public Beach
strings.d4.s1.tips: A tiny 18-metre beach run by Muratpaşa Municipality at the foot of the Şirinyalı cliffs; you enter between the rocks via a wooden platform, and it is open 08:00-20:00 all summer. Tourists don't know it and locals swim here in the morning; there are showers and cabins, and entry is symbolic. The sea gets deep within 3 metres, there are no pebbles and the water is glass-clear.
strings.d4.s2.name: Uysal Antalya Kuyu Tandır
strings.d4.s2.tips: In Kışla neighbourhood, 5 minutes from the Clock Tower; a well-oven tandır and soup place open 24 hours. Lamb cooked 4-5 hours in the well-oven is served on pide, with lentil soup and onion-parsley on the side; portions are big, and one and a half portions are enough for two. Choose your cut of meat at the counter and ask for the lean section.
strings.d4.s3.name: Sefa Hamam
strings.d4.s3.tips: A 15th-century Seljuk-Ottoman hamam in Kaleiçi, the oldest still in operation; separate sections for women and men. The basic package (hamam, scrub and foam massage) is the smartest way to spend the hottest part of the day on marble; oil massage costs extra. Open Monday-Saturday 12:30-20:00, closed Sunday; arrange a time via WhatsApp on +90 532 526 94 07.
strings.d4.s4.name: Tophane Tea Garden
strings.d4.s4.tips: A cheap tea garden run by the Metropolitan Municipality just below Republic Square; the Yacht Marina, the Kaleiçi rooftops and the Beydağları mountains in one view. It is on Hürriyet's list of Türkiye's 10 best tea gardens, yet tourists tend to stay inside Kaleiçi. Tables are hard to find at sunset, so arrive at 18:30; tea is 40-50 TL, service is slow, so don't rush.
strings.d4.s5.name: Hasan Antalya Restaurant
strings.d4.s5.tips: In the same family since 1946, in a hidden garden courtyard on Cumhuriyet Street in the Zincirli Han area; the menu has passed from grandfather to grandson. Tandır and tahini piyaz are the classics, but come mainly for the tripe soup and lentil fava; the kabak tatlısı is homemade. Call at 19:00 to hold a courtyard table.
strings.d4.b0.name: Lara Fish House (Işıklar)
strings.d4.b0.tips: A fish restaurant with bay views on Tevfik Işık Street in Gençlik neighbourhood, at the end of Işıklar; Ekşi Sözlük calls it 'reasonably priced views'. Order grilled octopus and calamari stuffed with shrimp; reservations on 0242 313 13 99.
strings.d4.b1.name: Antalya Toy Museum
strings.d4.b1.tips: The Metropolitan Municipality's toy museum in an old harbour warehouse at Kaleiçi Marina; tin toys from the 1920s. Closed Monday, open 09:30-18:30; entry is symbolic or free.
strings.d5.s0.name: Termessos Ancient City
strings.d5.s0.tips: In Güllük Mountain National Park in Döşemealtı, at 1,050 metres, this is the city Alexander the Great could not take; Türkiye's most dramatic ancient theatre sits at the cliff edge. Open 08:00-19:00 in summer; from the park gate it is 9 km of mountain road to the site, then a steep 20-minute climb from the car park. Start before 09:00: there is pine shade but humidity is high. Entry is 3 € plus a vehicle fee, and the Museum Pass is valid; the toppled sarcophagi in the necropolis make the strongest photo.
strings.d5.s1.name: Muhtarın Yeri Çakırlar
strings.d5.s1.tips: The Çakırlar valley in Kepez is where Antalya locals go for weekend village breakfast; this place, opened by the former village head in 1998, was the first in the valley. Village women roll gözleme on the griddle (spinach and cheese, potato), with honey and kaymak and tea over a wood fire; it fits perfectly as a late breakfast after Termessos. Quiet on weekdays; at weekends there is a queue after 10:00, and cash is preferred.
strings.d5.s2.name: Upper Düden Waterfall (Düdenbaşı)
strings.d5.s2.tips: In Varsak, Kepez, where the Düden Stream falls 15 metres; you can walk into the cave behind the waterfall and look out through the water, which Lower Düden doesn't offer. Nature park entry is about 100-150 TL, with a picnic area and cafés in plane-tree shade. The cave is slippery, so sea shoes help; in the midday heat this is the coolest corner of the city.
strings.d5.s3.name: Kırkgöz Lake
strings.d5.s3.tips: An ice-cold lake beside the Burdur road in Döşemealtı, formed by the karst springs that feed the Düden; right next to it stands the 13th-century Seljuk Kırkgöz Han. Locals brew tea on the shore in the early evening and dip their feet, and tourists rarely come. The han is often locked, but even its crown portal is worth seeing from outside.
strings.d5.s4.name: Yeşilbayır Ağar Restaurant
strings.d5.s4.tips: On Akdeniz Boulevard in Yeşilbayır, Döşemealtı, rated 4.3 on Google; an open-air pide and kebap hall where district families go to eat. Order minced-meat pide from the wood oven, lamb tandır and lahmacun; prices are half those in the centre. The way back to the city takes 25 minutes, and the garden is pleasant in the evening cool.
strings.d5.b0.name: Sedir Gözleme & Village Breakfast
strings.d5.b0.tips: The best-known gözleme place in Çakırlar; hand-rolled gözleme by local women, a sucuk-and-kaşar option and village butter. Busy at weekends, quiet on weekdays; ask for a table by the stream.
strings.d5.b1.name: Karain Cave
strings.d5.b1.tips: In Yağca village, Döşemealtı, Türkiye's most important Palaeolithic settlement; traces of human life 500,000 years old. It is a 15-minute climb up steps from the car park to the cave, and it is cool inside; entry is 5 € and the Museum Pass is valid.
strings.d6.s0.name: Köprülü Canyon National Park
strings.d6.s0.tips: Antalya's most popular activity: 14 km and 10 rapids on the Köprüçay north of Manavgat, in ice-cold spring water; you pass under the Roman-era Oluk Bridge. The shuttle picks you up from your hotel around 08:00, the canyon takes 1.5-2 hours, lunch by the river is included and you return at 17:00-18:00. Bring a waterproof phone pouch, clothes you don't mind getting wet and a change of clothes; a 4.9-rated Turkish-run tour starts at around 1,100 TL.
strings.d6.s1.name: Işıklar Street
strings.d6.s1.tips: The street where Antalya locals take their evening stroll; a palm-lined promenade, old Antalya cafés and ice-cream shops. Shake off the rafting tiredness with a coffee and ice cream; the street leads up to Atatürk Park on the cliff. Tourists stay in Kaleiçi, while this is the local evening rhythm.
strings.d6.s2.name: Atatürk Park
strings.d6.s2.tips: The city's oldest park, stretching along the cliff top beside Konyaaltı Street; sunset over Konyaaltı Bay and the Beydağları mountains is free. The benches face west and locals bring tea in thermoses. For photos, pick the middle platform that looks over the bay between the palms.
strings.d6.s3.name: Göz Balık
strings.d6.s3.tips: A modern fish restaurant on Lara Street in Şirinyalı, listed in the Gault & Millau Türkiye guide; 4.8 on Tripadvisor. Meze come from the counter and the fish of the day is priced by the gram; marinated sea bass and fried shrimp stand out, and one medium fish plus 4 meze is enough for two. Reserve on 0543 529 99 86; cards accepted.
strings.d6.b0.name: Nejat Balık (Şirinyalı)
strings.d6.b0.tips: On Old Lara Road beside Manavoğlu Park, a fish restaurant Antalya locals have used for years; open 09:00-00:00. Fried calamari and the grilled fish of the day are the classics; choose from the meze tray.
strings.d6.b1.name: Falez Park
strings.d6.b1.tips: A park with walking paths and viewing terraces on the Konyaaltı cliffs; think of it as the western continuation of Atatürk Park. The bay view at sunset is just as strong, with fewer people.
strings.d7.s0.name: Botanik Restaurant Ulupınar
strings.d7.s0.tips: On the Kemer-Finike road in Ulupınar village, just before the Olympos turn-off; tables sit in wooden pavilions over an ice-cold stream, at a place run by a family that has had a trout farm since 1990. Order the village breakfast (sac böreği, eggs, honey and kaymak) and dip your feet in the stream; trout is also an option for lunch on the way back. It is 1 hour 15 minutes from the centre, so leave at 07:30.
strings.d7.s1.name: Olympos Ancient City
strings.d7.s1.tips: Enter from the Çıralı side and you use the quiet gate instead of the crowded guesthouse valley; the Lycian-Roman city spreads over both banks of the stream, with ivy-covered sarcophagi and a necropolis. Open 08:00-21:00 in summer, entry 10 € (Museum Pass valid); on the path through the stream bed you may see turtles and crabs. You can walk straight from the site to the beach, so leave the car at the Çıralı car park.
strings.d7.s2.name: Çıralı Beach
strings.d7.s2.tips: A 3 km pebble-and-sand beach with orange groves and guesthouses behind it; as a nesting area for loggerhead (caretta caretta) turtles, it has no beach clubs, tall buildings or noise. The northern end where the Olympos ruins finish is the least crowded, with clear, deep water. Don't touch the marker stakes on turtle nests, and set up your umbrella on the sea side of the nest line.
strings.d7.s3.name: Yavuz Restaurant Çıralı
strings.d7.s3.tips: One of only two restaurants on the Çıralı seafront because of the building ban; simple menu under an arbour, feet in the sand. Order gözleme, a seasonal salad and the grilled fish of the day, with ayran and watermelon, for a light farewell lunch. Prices are those of a guesthouse village, so bring cash; if you leave at 15:00 you reach Antalya by 17:00.
strings.d7.b0.name: Azur Restaurant Çıralı
strings.d7.b0.tips: Çıralı's best-known restaurant, with Mediterranean cooking and fresh seafood in a garden near the beach. The grilled sea bass and meze are good; book a table for weekend lunch.
strings.d7.b1.name: Phaselis Ancient City
strings.d7.b1.tips: A Lycian port city with three bays near Tekirova; the two ends of the ancient main street open onto two separate bays, and you can swim among the ruins in pine shade. Entry 10 €, Museum Pass valid; the north bay is the calmest.
strings.note0: Payment: Cards work in Kaleiçi and seafront restaurants, but tradesmen's lokantas, the Çakırlar breakfast places and the Fishing Harbour counters mostly want cash; carry 2,000-3,000 TL in cash.
strings.note1: Transport: Within the city, buses and trams (AntRay/Nostalgia) with an Antalyakart are enough; the Lara, Aksu and Konyaaltı lines run frequently. For the Termessos, Köprülü and Olympos days you need to rent a car or use dolmuşes from the bus station.
strings.note2: Tipping: 5-10% is enough in restaurants and is not expected in tradesmen's lokantas. At the hamam, a separate tip of 100-200 TL for the attendant is customary.
strings.note3: Dress: At the ancient cities (Termessos, Perge, Olympos) you need closed shoes, a hat and at least 1.5 L of water; there is no shade. Shoulders and knees must be covered when entering mosques (Fluted Minaret, Tekeli Mehmet Pasha).
strings.note4: Season warning: In July it reaches 38-40°C between 12:00 and 15:00; finish the ancient cities by 08:30 and spend midday in the sea or shade. The sea is around 28°C, and the evening cool arrives after 20:30.
strings.note5: Safety: At cliff beaches (like Erdal Inönü) rock and depth begin suddenly, so enter via the wooden platform; at the cliff edge where the Düden Waterfall meets the sea, don't climb over the railing. Life jackets and helmets are compulsory for rafting.
strings.note6: Local etiquette: In Antalya piyaz is made with tahini and comes alongside köfte as a main meze, not as a 'salad'; tea at Tophane is drunk slowly from a glass, and coffee in Kaleiçi from a small cup. In Çakırlar a table is held for a two-hour breakfast chat, and nobody hurries.
strings.niche.name: Antalya Fishing Harbour
strings.niche.why_hidden: At the western end of Konyaaltı, next to the commercial port, this is a working fishing harbour run by two fisheries cooperatives (S.S. Yeni Liman and S.S. Yeşil Antalya); coastal boats dock in the morning and fish is sold directly at the cooperative counter. Tourist guides describe Konyaaltı as beaches and beach clubs, and don't mention that 500 metres away there are craftsmen mending nets and a morning auction; this is Antalya's real fishing neighbourhood.
strings.niche.access_instructions: At the entrance to Liman neighbourhood on the Antalya-Kemer road; take a Kemer-direction bus from the centre (Antalyakart) to the 'Liman' stop, then walk 5 minutes. The cooperative office and fish sales are open weekdays 08:30-17:30 and Saturday 08:30-12:30, closed Sunday; the liveliest time is 08:30-09:30 as the boats dock. You can walk freely on the quay, but don't board boats without permission.
strings.niche.insider_tip: When buying fish at the cooperative counter, say 'clean and ice it' (temizleyip buzlayın); they do it free, and cooking it that evening on the grills at the Sarısu picnic area is a local habit. If you strike up a 'what came out this morning' chat with the fishermen at the tea stand beside the counter, they will tell you which Konyaaltı cove has clear water that week and which days are windy.
strings.niche.season: Year-round; however, during the 15 April-1 September trawl and purse-seine fishing ban only small coastal boats go out, so the counter has less variety but still offers red mullet, sea bream, squid and shrimp. The counter is fullest from September to April.
strings.transit.name: Antalyakart
strings.transit.why_chosen: The one card that works on all of Antalya's municipal buses, the AntRay tram and the Nostalgia tram; where a single-use ticket costs 46 TL and tapping a credit card costs 50 TL, a ride with Antalyakart is 42 TL, and the transfer discount exists only on this card. Every Kaleiçi, Konyaaltı, Lara, Aksu and Varsak stop in the plan is on an Antalyakart line; for the Termessos, Köprülü and Olympos days you need a car or a dolmuş from the bus station, and the card won't get you there. One card is enough for two people over 7 days, as it can be tapped twice.
